page: Amazon Web Services c6id.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this server provides 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It operates at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz and features a 54 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 192 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

This instance features 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, providing high-speed local read and write capabilities directly attached via the Nitro hypervisor. It does not include a dedicated GPU. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 38 Gbps, facilitating rapid data transfer for distributed workloads.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. The hardware excels in cryptographic tasks, with the Passmark CPU encryption test reaching the top 10% tier, and Geekbench ray tracing also scoring in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks consistently rank in the top 25%. However, single-core performance benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core, fall in the middle 50% average tier. Large-scale LLM inference, specifically text generation with a 70B model, is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25%.

From a resource density perspective, the c6id.24xlarge offers a dense allocation of compute resources and high-capacity local NVMe storage relative to its hardware class, making it a viable option for workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space without the overhead of network-attached storage. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and software compilation.
